solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree French author felled?

indicators.note: a felled tree is laid flat, so the author's name is turned and read the other way

parts.note: Albert Camus, French novelist of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A lumberjack joke: a French writer cut down like a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felled' turns CAMUS round to give the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sumac is a shrub or small tree whose leaves and berries are used for dye and spice.

clue.text: Fruit salad to begin with, then fish

indicators.note: to begin with asks for only the opening letter

parts.note: haddock is a fish

explanation.surface: A menu: fruit salad first, then a fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: A large citrus fruit, the pomelo, also called by this name.

clue.text: Chaos in a Sicilian city

parts.note: a mess is chaos
taken as written

explanation.surface: Disorder in a town in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the north-east tip of Sicily, across the strait from mainland Italy.

clue.text: Hit on the head — or nose

definitions.meaning: informal verb for a blow to the skull

explanation.surface: A punch landing on the head or the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for a blow to the head and for the nose itself.

clue.text: Greatly impress an admirer of the East End?

definitions.text: an admirer of the East End?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a fan of Bow, a district of London's East End

explanation.surface: Charming a fan of London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district in the East End of London, home of the Bow Bells, so a lover of it is a 'Bow lover'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to astonish or overwhelm someone with admiration.

clue.text: Translation of Navaho and Rumanian book

indicators.note: a translation puts words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A text rendered from two languages, Navajo and Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's 1958 spy novel set in Cuba.

clue.text: Opera in state capital only showing second half

indicators.note: only the latter half of the city's name appears, the first half dropped

parts.note: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii

explanation.surface: An opera playing in a US state capital, only the second half shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg's unfinished twentieth-century opera.

clue.text: Papal authority to have vessels laden with incense, primarily

indicators.note: laden with means carrying something inside

parts.note: a vat and a can are both vessels

indicators.note: primarily takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: The Church needing containers full of incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laden with' sets the single letter between the two containers; 'primarily' picks the first letter of incense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's government, is named after his Roman palace.

clue.text: Damned healthy-looking

definitions.meaning: a mild British expletive, as in a bloody nuisance

explanation.surface: A grudging remark about someone's glowing health.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a euphemistic curse and a description of a florid, rosy face.

clue.text: Sweeping movement of men like so?

definitions.meaning: chessmen or draughtsmen move over the board

explanation.surface: A sweeping shift of personnel, of men moved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' are pieces in chess or draughts, which move over the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means applying to all, comprehensive, as in pay rises for everyone.

clue.text: Poison found in medicines, rarely recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A toxin that turns up only seldom in medicines that have been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Poison found' as the definition, but 'found in' is the signal for the concealed letters; the definition is 'Poison' alone. 'recalled' turns CINESRA round.
explanation.definitionFit: This element and its compounds are a classic poison of murder mysteries.

clue.text: At first, really happy to get connected

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: elated means very happy

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at last getting online.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are linked by kinship or logic are said to be connected.

clue.text: Party elected to kill

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A political party voted in on a mandate to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means to murder or finish someone off.

clue.text: Comfortable thing, right to this point

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable seat

explanation.surface: Someone saying their comfy settee has been fine up till now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up until now, as far as things have gone.

clue.text: Ill having missed starter, too sweet

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, as a diner skipping the first course

parts.note: dicky is British informal for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: A diner feeling sick after skipping the first course and finding dessert cloying.
explanation.walkthrough: DICKY is British slang for unsound or poorly; 'having missed starter' drops its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something sickly sentimental or cloying is described this way.

clue.text: Trifle to be held over a basin

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part above the second

parts.note: to trifle is to play, toy

explanation.surface: A dessert set to rest above a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry desert basin that floods into a shallow lake after rain.

clue.text: Fish skim over the surface

definitions.meaning: glide over ice or deal superficially

explanation.surface: A fish darting along the top of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish and the verb for gliding on ice.

clue.text: Author reads novel about legendary leader among poltroons

indicators.note: among places the built group within the cowards' word

parts.note: poltroons are cowards, informally chickens

indicators.note: about wraps the shuffled letters round the single letter
novel means new or unusual, signalling the letters of reads are rearranged
the leader of legendary is its first letter

explanation.surface: A writer reading a novel about a mythic chief among cowards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' shuffles the letters to ARESD, and 'about' wraps them round L to make ARLESD, the piece that goes 'among' the cowards.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Victorian novelist who wrote Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

clue.text: All off, one off?

parts.note: one with all clothes off who runs off at speed, as at a sports ground

explanation.surface: A cryptic riddle about stripping and running.
explanation.walkthrough: The naked runner who dashes across a pitch has 'all off' (clothes) and is 'off' (running).
explanation.definitionFit: A naked person dashing through a public place, typically a sports match.

clue.text: Be an axe murderer — or make peace?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, to sink a small axe into someone
the idiom for ending a quarrel

explanation.surface: A grim choice between violence and reconciliation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a Native American custom of laying down weapons to end hostilities.

clue.text: So save more scrap

definitions.meaning: read as two words, therefore consume less

explanation.surface: Economy advice: recycle waste to cut costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthless junk, of no further value, is fit only for the scrap heap.

clue.text: Anything but her Labour background?

parts.note: the opposite of her is his
the 'anything but' carries over: the opposite of a Labour politician is a Conservative

explanation.surface: A woman's political past not in the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and the Tories are the two main British parties, so 'anything but Labour' gives TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's past experience or record forms their background.

clue.text: Mock gemstones in one's shop, well hidden

indicators.note: hidden here means kept out of sight, so that word is removed

parts.note: one who has gems in their shop is a jeweller
taken as written

explanation.surface: Laughing at the jewels a shopkeeper keeps tucked out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove WELL from JEWELLER to leave the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride or taunt someone, synonym of mock as a verb.

clue.text: Account penned by one biblical character — for another?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: Job of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A chronicle written by one Bible figure about another.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac's son, father of the twelve tribes, is a second Old Testament figure.

clue.text: US president storing old volume on the next floor up?

indicators.note: storing means holding something inside

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Lincoln keeping an ancient book upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the floor overhead is located higher up, a positional sense.

clue.text: Man, say I do crosswords regularly?

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: to solve is what one does with crosswords

explanation.surface: A man mentioning that he does puzzles from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man, say' is the Isle of Man, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is an example of such a small island.

clue.text: All initially in the soup, appointing rotten old Russian leader

indicators.note: all initially means take the first letter of every word that follows

explanation.surface: Everyone in trouble because of a corrupt appointment by a former ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' is British for in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor of pre-revolutionary Russia.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of a plant

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk holding up a plant

explanation.surface: A loyal backer of a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stop a flow, and the noun is the main stalk of a plant.

clue.text: Tea houses otherwise in place of buns?

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A teashop serving something besides buns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chelsea bun is a rolled currant bun named after the London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The district of west London gives its name to a famous spiral currant bun.

clue.text: Arrangement to switch all seats marked J perhaps with K

indicators.note: to switch here means to turn the row round end to end

parts.note: J is the tenth letter, so seats lettered J make up row ten

explanation.surface: A theatre manager reallocating the J seats to row K.
explanation.walkthrough: J is the tenth letter of the alphabet, so row J is ROW TEN; 'to switch' turns it round to NETWOR, then K is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A system or pattern of interconnected lines or parts is an arrangement.

clue.text: Bridge ace takes journey

parts.note: ace means excellent, the best
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A card player's trump card winning a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' is the verb: to span or straddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle or span something, as a bridge spans a river.

clue.text: Wander over to collect unknown civic dignitary

indicators.note: to collect means taking something in
over in a down-across sense means turned back

parts.note: to roam is to wander
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A local official taking an unplanned walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROAM to MAOR, which takes in Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a town council is its chief civic official.
